gap: Manual Call Point (MCP) found blocked, with no signage indicating its location.
recommendation: Immediately clear access to the MCP and provide clear, illuminated location signage; include MCP accessibility in routine safety-inspection checklists.

gap: Emergency exit sign lights are not installed.
recommendation: Install illuminated (or photoluminescent, battery- backed) emergency exit signage at all designated exits and verify functionality during periodic fire-safety inspections.

gap: Self-contained battery-backup beam lights are not installed in the work area.
recommendation: Install battery-backed emergency lighting in all operational areas to ensure safe evacuation during power failure; include in the preventive-maintenance and testing schedule.

gap: Evacuation maps are not placed in work areas.
recommendation: Develop and post area-specific evacuation maps showing exit routes, assembly points, and MCP/extinguisher locations at all entrances and common areas.

gap: Emergency exit directional signs/arrows are not posted.
recommendation: Install directional evacuation signage along all egress routes leading to exits and muster points.

gap: Fire extinguisher placed on the ground, hidden among plant pots, and not identified with flag-type signage.
recommendation: Relocate the extinguisher to an unobstructed, clearly visible wall-mounted or stand location and install flag/location signage above it; repeat the check across all extinguisher points.

gap: Visitor cards do not carry an emergency contact number.
recommendation: Redesign the visitor card/badge to include the site emergency contact number and basic emergency- response instructions.
remarks: In-progress with FFC PQ Admin & Security

gap: Smoking area is not formally designated.
recommendation: Designate, sign-post, and provide appropriate fire- safety controls (e.g., ashtrays, distance from flammable storage) for a formal smoking area; communicate the policy to staff and visitors.

gap: Rubber insulation mats are not placed in front of electrical panels.
recommendation: Install rated rubber matting at all LV/HV panel access points and include mat condition in routine electrical-safety inspections.
remarks:
Mat availbale but limited in quantity, need to be enhanced.
 As per the current operational requirements the Mats are fulfilling the purpose. At a time work is being performed on one starter/panel/cubicle.
 However, new Mats procurement has been budgeted for the next year. Kindly, close the point.
 
 These mats are placed in secure controlled environment and are being inspected visually regularly.

gap: Electrical hazard warning signs with voltage rating are not posted on the electrical panels.
recommendation: Install standardised hazard/voltage-rating signage on every electrical panel; verify as part of the electrical- safety audit checklist.
remarks: Hazard/voltage rating tags have been pasted on the electrical panels. Point to be closed.

gap: Electrical safety rubber gloves were found without expiry dates, the team was not aware of the validity requirement, and no dielectric test reports were available to confirm the PPE remains safe to use.
recommendation: Institute a periodic dielectric test regime for insulating gloves (e.g., every six months per applicable standard), label each pair with test/expiry dates, retain test certificates, and train users on validity requirements.
remarks: Testing facilty to be searched.

gap: An unidentified, live electrical panel with connected wiring was found outside the carpentry shop next to a pile of wooden pieces.
recommendation: Immediately relocate combustible material away from the panel, label/identify the panel and its circuits, and secure it against unauthorised access; treat as a fire-risk priority item.

gap: A list of earth pits has not been developed.
recommendation: Compile and maintain a master list of all earth pits with location references, and incorporate periodic earth-resistance testing into the maintenance/calibration programme.
remarks:
Marked on Drawing. 
 List needs to be developed
 The annual earth resistance testing sheet is attached as evidence that the subject pits/earth bars are having distinct numbers.
 Point to be closed.

gap: Underground cable ducts are not covered.
recommendation: Install and secure protective covers over all open cable ducts to eliminate trip/fall and cable-damage hazards; inspect periodically.

gap: Extension cords and multi-plug adapters are in use without prior assessment or load calculation.
recommendation:
Establish a control on temporary electrical connections requiring risk assessment/load calculation and approval before use, and phase out uncontrolled multi-plug use in favour of fixed outlets where
 feasible.

gap: Oil drums/canes found without secondary containment.
recommendation: Provide bunded/secondary containment (capacity ≥110% of the largest container) for all oil and chemical drum storage areas to prevent uncontrolled spills.

gap: No hazard-identification labels found on drums/canes.
recommendation:
Label all chemical/oil containers with standardised hazard pictograms and content identification (GHS-
 aligned), cross-referenced to MSDS.

gap: MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheets) are not found/posted in the area where oil/chemicals are stored.
recommendation: Compile and post current MSDS at each storage/use point and maintain a master MSDS register accessible to all relevant staff.

gap: No spill kits found in the oil/chemical storage area.
recommendation: Provide spill-response kits sized to the largest credible spill at each storage location, and train staff on their use as part of emergency-response drills.

gap: A trench provided in the oil/storage area leads spills directly into the sewer system.
recommendation: Redirect or seal the trench so it no longer provides a pathway to the sewer/stormwater system; install an oil-water separator or containment sump, and assess whether any historical discharge requires remediation or regulatory notification.

gap: Waste canes/oil/batteries/tyres and filters found unidentified at the rear of the oil storage area.
recommendation: Establish designated, labelled waste-segregation points for each waste stream (used oil, batteries, tyres, filters) with appropriate secondary containment, consistent with the Waste Management procedure (MRO-SP-HSE-007).

gap: Flood/detention tanks require cleaning and clear demarcation of area jurisdiction/ownership.
recommendation: Schedule periodic cleaning/desilting of flood tanks and assign clear departmental ownership with marked boundaries and a defined inspection frequency.

gap: One fixed grinder found without a safety guard/cover.
recommendation: Fit an appropriate machine guard before the grinder is returned to service; include guard presence in routine equipment safety checks.

gap: Sharp tools found stored without any safety protocol.
recommendation: Introduce a sharps-storage protocol (dedicated racks/sheaths, restricted access) and train staff on safe storage and handling.

gap: No ladder-inspection mechanism found.
recommendation: Implement a periodic ladder-inspection programme (pre-use and scheduled checks) with tagging/colour-coding to indicate current inspection status.

gap: A list of confined spaces has not been developed and identified.
recommendation: Conduct a confined-space survey, maintain a register of identified spaces, and implement entry controls (permit-to-work, atmospheric testing, standby person) for each.
remarks: List is developed and under signing

gap: PPE not found in some areas, or PPE provided was not relevant to the task/operation being performed.
recommendation: Conduct a task-based PPE needs assessment for each work area, ensure availability of the correct PPE at point of use, and reinforce compliance through supervisory checks.

gap: Hygiene and medical screening records for canteen staff/food handlers are not available.
recommendation: Institute periodic medical/hygiene screening for food handlers per applicable food-safety/occupational- health requirements and maintain records centrally.

gap: First aid boxes lack the prescribed kit/list per civil-defence protocols, and injectable medicines were found stored in first aid boxes, which should only be issued by a qualified medical practitioner.
recommendation: Standardise first-aid box contents against the prescribed checklist, remove injectable/prescription medicines from unsupervised boxes, and route their issuance through the site medical clinic/qualified practitioner only.

gap: Daily motor-vehicle inspection sheets are not controlled (as documented information).
recommendation: Bring vehicle inspection sheets under document control (numbering, revision, retention) consistent with the Documentation procedure.

gap: One forklift indicator was found non- operational, yet the daily inspection sheet recorded it as satisfactory.
recommendation: Take the forklift out of service until repaired, retrain the inspecting operator on defect-reporting requirements, and introduce a supervisory spot-check on inspection-sheet accuracy.

gap: Daily motor-vehicle inspection sheets are not checked/verified by a second party (verifier).
recommendation: Introduce a supervisor/verifier sign-off step on the daily inspection sheet before the vehicle is released for use.

gap: Multimeter calibration tag expiry date does not match the calibration report.
recommendation: Reconcile calibration tags against certificates for all instruments and correct the discrepancy; add a verification step when tags are issued.

gap: Calibration tag found missing on a weighing scale.
recommendation: Tag the weighing scale with current calibration status and due date; include it in the master calibration list.
remarks: Updated calibration tag are attached to the equipment as evidence.

gap: One weight (mass standard) used with the analytical weighing balance showed a deviated value in the third-party calibration report, and the weight itself was not marked, risking miscalculation by the user.
recommendation: Mark the weight with its as-found deviation/correction value (or withdraw it from service if outside tolerance) and update the calibration record accordingly.
remarks: Deviated value updated on Tag

gap: The user was not able to demonstrate the procedure for performing a weight test on the analytical weighing balance.
recommendation: Provide documented work instructions and hands-on training for weight-test/verification procedures, and verify competence periodically.
remarks: Training will be provided to each individual.

gap: The operator was not able to fully demonstrate the safety inspection protocols for the equipment operated.
recommendation: Reinforce operator training on safety inspection protocols and verify competence through periodic practical assessment.

gap: A complaint-handling mechanism was found not to be intact or documented in some areas.
recommendation: Deploy a standardised, documented complaint- handling procedure across all areas, with a defined logging, investigation, and closure process.

gap: A temperature monitor is installed in the turbine area and the online inspection sheet is meant to confirm control-room temperature stays within specified limits; however, control-room operators are not recording temperature readings at the required interval (once per 8-hour shift).
recommendation: Reinforce the recording requirement with operators/shift supervisors, and consider automated logging/alarming for the temperature monitor to reduce reliance on manual entries.
remarks: Reading is already noted in FHCK. Requirement of addition of note in digital FHCK that readig will be noted once a shift is shared with FHCK IT Team.

gap: The cable room is not kept free of unrelated storage, and cable trays are not maintained clean and tidy.
recommendation: Clear the cable room of unrelated stored items, implement a housekeeping standard for cable trays, and include the area in routine housekeeping inspections.
remarks:
Proper Housekeeping has been carried out.
 Point to be closed

gap: No FIFO/FEFO/LIFO stock-rotation system is in place.
recommendation: Select and implement an appropriate stock-rotation methodology (e.g., FIFO/FEFO) suited to the material type, and train store/inventory staff accordingly.

gap: No fire alarm system inspection record is maintained.
recommendation: Implement a periodic fire-alarm-system inspection/testing regime (per applicable fire code) and maintain records centrally.
remarks: Annual Testing sheet is attached as evidence. Point to be closed.

gap: No fire extinguisher inspection record is maintained.
recommendation: Implement monthly (or as required) fire-extinguisher inspection checks with a logged record, tag, and defined replacement/refill cycle.

gap: No consolidated list of calibrated equipment exists.
recommendation: Develop and maintain a master list of all equipment requiring calibration, including calibration frequency and responsible party.

gap: No list of equipment requiring load testing has been developed.
recommendation: Identify all lifting/load-bearing equipment requiring periodic load testing and compile a master list with testing intervals.

gap: Load-testing reports from a LEEA- approved inspector are not available for all respective lifting equipment.
recommendation: Arrange periodic load testing of lifting equipment through a LEEA-approved (or equivalent accredited) inspector and retain certificates as documented information.

gap: No list of equipment requiring environmental testing has been developed.
recommendation: Identify equipment/parameters requiring environmental testing (emissions, effluent, noise, etc.) and compile a master monitoring list.
remarks: Environmental Management Plan is available & All Parameters as per SEQS are maintained in compliance

gap: No environmental testing plan exists covering ambient air, lux, noise, gaseous emissions, drinking water, and waste water against SEQS parameters, using a SEPA-approved laboratory.
recommendation: Develop and implement an annual environmental monitoring plan covering all applicable SEQS parameters, using a SEPA-accredited laboratory, with defined frequencies and reporting/record-retention requirements.
remarks: The same is covered under EMP plan and is being followed religiously. Point to be closed

gap: No energy consumption record (renewable energy, diesel, natural gas, water, etc.) has been maintained for the past year.
recommendation: Establish a utility/energy consumption tracking system covering all major energy and water sources, retroactively compiling the past year's data where available, to support EMS performance evaluation and objectives.
remarks: Standard document for the same is Flash & Material Balance report and is being maintained by Operations

gap: No inventory of ozone-depleting substances (ODS) has been maintained for the past year.
recommendation: Compile an ODS inventory (types, quantities, locations, e.g., refrigerants) and establish a process for tracking use, leaks, and disposal.
remarks: Not Pertain to PE Unit

gap: The monitoring and measurement system needs to be enhanced and formally documented.
recommendation: Define what is monitored, at what frequency, by whom, and how results are analysed/evaluated at process and IMS-wide levels; document this in a Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis and Evaluation procedure (see Clause 9.1.1 recommendation, Section 4).

gap: A list of internal and external documents has not been developed.
recommendation: Compile a master list of internal documents and external documents (standards, legal texts, customer specifications) as part of the Documentation procedure's document register.
remarks: Internal and external document list being maintained in PSM PSI.

gap: Document levels/hierarchy are not defined within the document and data control procedure.
recommendation: Define a document hierarchy (e.g., Manual > Procedures > Work Instructions > Forms/Records) within the Documentation procedure (MRO-SP-IMS- 001) and apply it consistently across the IMS document set.

gap: Personal files are not consistently available with appropriate job descriptions (JD) and relevant educational/experience documents.
recommendation: Standardise personnel files to include an approved JD and supporting educational/experience credentials for every employee, and periodically audit for completeness.
remarks: All personal files, along with the respective Job Descriptions (JDs) and relevant educational and experience documents, are maintained by Head Office HR. PDF copies are provided to Local HR upon request.

gap: Not all drivers have valid and relevant driving licences on record.
recommendation: Verify and record valid, category-appropriate driving licences for all drivers before permitting vehicle operation, and track renewal dates.

gap: Refresher training (technical and safety protocols) is not consistently provided to all staff.
recommendation: Develop a refresher-training calendar covering technical and safety topics for all relevant roles, with attendance and competence records maintained centrally.
remarks: No separate calender is required, refresher trainings as per HSE requirements are already included in annual training calendar, however, compliance from HSE and end users are required to improved.

gap: A formal training plan has not been developed or shared with staff.
recommendation: Develop an annual training plan (linked to a competence/training-needs analysis, once developed) and communicate it to staff and department heads.
remarks: TNA is already being followed and annual training plan is developed accordingly. Training calendars for both FPCL and FFC-PQ are shared with training coordinators in June 2026. Refer attached annual caledars for FFC-PQ and FPCL for understanding.

gap: A supplier evaluation procedure has not been developed, and supplier evaluations are not conducted against approved criteria.
recommendation: Develop a Control of External Providers procedure defining evaluation, selection, and re-evaluation criteria (as recommended in Section 6.2), and begin conducting evaluations against it.

gap: An approved supplier list has not been developed.
recommendation: Compile and maintain an approved supplier list, updated following each supplier evaluation cycle.

gap: No formal Service Level Agreement (SLA) is in place for shared services received from FFC-PQ (Laboratory, Fire Department, and Medical Clinic).
recommendation: Formalise SLAs with FFC-PQ for each shared service, defining scope, response times, and performance indicators, and review periodically.

gap: A list of chemicals used/stored on site has not been developed.
recommendation: Compile a master chemicals inventory (linked to MSDS) covering all chemicals used or stored on site, and keep it current.
remarks: Is already being maintained.

gap: A list of required PPE has not been developed.
recommendation: Develop a task/role-based PPE matrix specifying required PPE per activity, to support the PPE gap noted at OBS-31.

gap: A list of required safety equipment has not been developed.
recommendation: Compile a master list of required safety equipment (fire, first-aid, spill-response, rescue, etc.) by location, cross-referenced to inspection/maintenance schedules.

gap: Inventory records have not been fully developed.
recommendation: Establish a complete inventory record-keeping system covering raw materials, spares, and consumables, integrated with the stock-rotation control recommended at OBS-38.

gap: The Permit-to-Work (PTW) system (covering hot work, cold work, work at height, etc.) needs to be checked/verified for effective implementation.
recommendation: Audit the PTW system against its defined procedure for all applicable work categories, close any gaps identified, and reinforce permit-issuer/receiver training.

gap: Departmental objectives have not been developed as SMART objectives with explicit reference to the Integrated Management System.
recommendation: Cascade IMS-level objectives (per MRO-SP-IMS-004) into SMART departmental objectives, cross-referenced to the master objectives register.

gap: The list of interested parties needs to be reviewed.
recommendation: Review and update the interested-parties register (recommended at Clause 4.2, Section 4) to ensure it reflects current internal and external stakeholders and their requirements.

gap: Issues of concern (internal/external context issues) need to be reviewed.
recommendation: Conduct/refresh the context-of-the-organization analysis (recommended at Clause 4.1, Section 4) to formally capture and periodically review relevant internal and external issues.
